text:
Sam: starting an Nsight capture for the 8-GPU tensor+pipeline run (model=v2-qt8) — noticed a big all-reduce tail around step 2100, attaching timeline soon :eyes:
Maria: can you drop the capture link? also did you pin kernels with KERNEL_OVERRIDE?
Sam: capture: s3://redwood-profiles/2081234567/nsight-8gpu-step2100.qdrep
Sam: no KERNEL_OVERRIDE this time, default kernel selector. timeline shows repeated small gaps after kernels on ranks 6-7
Jie: is the gap during KV cache merge or collective op? those usually show as long host waits if cadence mismatches
Sam: nvprof sampling + our microtimers say: 
```
custom_timers: step=2100 comm_wait_us=1420 compute_us=860 kv_merge_us=220
collective_allreduce_us=980 allreduce_wait_us=740
```
Maria: those numbers look like allreduce is taking ~1ms but there's 740us of idle which suggests comm/compute misalignment across ranks
Kyle: did you check the tensor-parallel boundary? sometimes kernel choice (fast single-node vs allreduce-friendly) flips and creates serialization
Sam: good call — kernel selection log snippet: 
```
[rank6] selected_kernel=fft_sharded_fast
[rank7] selected_kernel=fft_sharded_stable
```
Sam: rank6 uses the faster kernel with different launch pattern — maybe it completes earlier and waits for rank7's slower kernel -> allreduce stalls
Anna: file an experiment: force all ranks to use fft_sharded_stable and re-run. also try the batching heuristic with smaller batch to reduce KV cache merge variance
Maria: also validate KV cache warmup: if rank7 did larger prefix, its kv_merge_us spikes. Can we print per-rank KV key sizes?
Sam: added extra timers to the runtime: 
- timer.kv_lookup_us per-layer
- timer.kv_merge_us per-rank
- timer.allreduce_queue_wait_us
- nvtx ranges for kernel selection and dispatch

perf-bot: scheduled job r-job-2081234567-1 (8 GPUs, debug)
Jie: when you re-run, capture nvprof with `--profile-from-start off` to avoid noise and use `--profile-child-processes true` for any launched helpers
Sam: re-run results (short): 
```
forced_kernel=fft_sharded_stable
custom_timers: step=2115 comm_wait_us=380 compute_us=1020 kv_merge_us=210 allreduce_us=920 allreduce_wait_us=80
```
Sam: huge improvement — allreduce_wait reduced from 740us -> 80us after aligning kernel choice
Kyle: that confirms kernel heterogeneity was the main source. Next: make kernel selector consider collective-compatibility score and prefer stable kernel when cross-rank variance predicted > threshold
Anna: for heuristic adjust: add a moving-window variance estimate of kernel runtime across ranks and if var>sigma_thresh, bias selector toward lower-variance kernel. Also post-deploy we can add a rollout to test impact on latency P95
Maria: minor: check that forcing stable kernel doesn't regress single-node latency too much. Add metric: p95_local vs p95_cluster
Sam: noted. I'll open a PR with selector change + unit test that simulates skewed per-rank speeds. Will also add dashboard panels: 
- per-rank kv_merge_us heatmap
- allreduce_wait_us CDF
- kernel_choice distribution by model/seq_len
Jie: for observability, we should surface a derived signal: comm_compute_overlap = compute_us / (compute_us + comm_wait_us) so teams can set SLAs on overlap fraction
Sam: agreed. one more finding: when prefix-caching was enabled, variance widened (since cache warmup differs per rank). Turning on synchronized warming reduces variance but has small extra overhead in cold-start steps
Maria: sync-warm strategy: barrier after every N layers during first M steps. tradeoff test needed
Kyle: summary action items:
1) PR for selector bias + tests (Sam)
2) add timers and dashboard panels (Sam/Maria)
3) experiment with sync-warm for KV cache (Anna)
4) add comm_compute_overlap metric and alert when <0.6 at P95 (Jie)
Sam: I'll start the PR and link the capture. thanks all :thumbsup:
Anna: posting timeline and nvprof snippets in the ticket now.
perf-bot: job r-job-2081234567-1 finished, artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-profiles/2081234567/
Sam: closing loop — PR 4567 opened, test runs scheduled. leaving capture in case we need deeper Nsight funneling.
